name: IEC binary decoder (X/Y coder)
summary: IEC coder marked BIN/OCT or similar, converting a binary input code into one active output.
description: IEC coders use the general qualifier X/Y, where X is the input code and Y is the output code. A three-to-eight-line decoder is therefore marked BIN/OCT, with input weights 1, 2 and 4 and outputs numbered 0 to 7. Enable inputs are often combined with an & element in the common-control area.

Decoders select one of several devices, relays or indicator lines from a binary code. A drawing should keep the output numbers so a reviewer can confirm that, for example, input code 5 activates output 5.
The qualifier says nothing about output polarity; polarity triangles at outputs show active-low outputs, which are common on decoder devices.
readingNotes: X/Y gives input and output codes.
Check output polarity marks before reading the truth table.
drawingChecklist: State the code pair, such as BIN/OCT.
distinction: A BCD/7SEG coder produces segment drive patterns, not one-of-n outputs.
